chunk-001:c001.proposition: Naturalism coherently integrates empirical science by treating the rule-governed natural world as reality while acknowledging unresolved questions about value, meaning, and purpose.

orphanFallback.rationale: Carroll presents this positive definition of naturalism and its acknowledged limits without depending on any preceding opposing claim.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Plausible eternal and finite self-contained cosmological models remove the need to invoke something outside nature as a mechanism for the universe's origin.

orphanFallback.rationale: The cited existence of self-contained cosmological models independently supports naturalism even if no earlier theistic compatibility claim is retained.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: If life requires rare conditions, environmental selection across a multiverse provides a naturalistic explanation, and such multiverses can follow from compact physical theories rather than ad hoc multiplication.

orphanFallback.rationale: Carroll's observer-selection mechanism and appeal to independently motivated physical theories constitute a freestanding naturalistic account of apparent fine-tuning.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Quantum mechanics revises the scientific description of matter but has no foundational implication that undermines materialism in the relevant metaphysical sense.

orphanFallback.rationale: The claim directly locates quantum theory within a materialist worldview and remains intelligible without an earlier opposing characterization of quantum mechanics.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Physical determinism is orthogonal to free will because choice can function legitimately as an emergent macroscopic concept even though it is absent from fundamental physical laws.

orphanFallback.rationale: Carroll constructs the view through an explicit analogy between choice and emergent quantities such as temperature, pressure, and entropy.

chunk-003:c003-01.proposition: Knowledge is best pursued through a revisable equilibrium among experience, coherent provisional principles, correction of human bias, and empirically successful scientific rules.

orphanFallback.rationale: Carroll offers this as a self-contained account of fallible inquiry in which principles remain answerable to experience and open to revision.

chunk-003:c003-04.proposition: Consciousness is a difficult unfinished neuroscience problem but presently gives no reason to abandon physicalism if brain states can be mapped to conscious reports and behavior.

orphanFallback.rationale: Treating consciousness as a tractable brain-mapping research program positively states physicalism's present explanatory approach without requiring the questioner's objection.

chunk-003:c003-05.proposition: Morality is constructed from human judgments and preferences rather than discovered as an external universal fact, since moral disputes lack decisive empirical tests.

orphanFallback.rationale: Carroll directly grounds moral philosophy in the systematization of human judgments, independently of any earlier opposing move.

chunk-003:c003-08.proposition: Naturalism intensifies earthly meaning because finite lives, relationships, and shared experiences are the only available locus of value rather than preparation for an afterlife.

orphanFallback.rationale: Carroll's finite-life account positively identifies relationships and shared experience as sources of meaning even without an earlier criticism of naturalist value.
